listening_script.speed_note: Read aloud at a normal, clear pace (85 wpm). Pause 2–3 seconds between sentences. Read the full text twice before students answer questions.
listening_script.text:
Sometimes, one cause leads to many effects. Or many causes lead to one effect.
This is called a CHAIN REACTION.
Example: The Pollution Chain
CAUSE 1: Factories produce smoke.
CAUSE 2: Cars produce exhaust.
↓
EFFECT: The air becomes polluted.
↓
EFFECT 2: People get sick.
↓
EFFECT 3: Hospitals become crowded.
We can write this as a paragraph:
"The air in big cities is polluted. This is because factories produce smoke.
Also, cars produce exhaust. As a result, many people get sick.
This leads to crowded hospitals. Therefore, we need to reduce pollution."
Notice the connectors:
- This is because... (introduces cause)
- Also... (adds another cause)
- As a result... (introduces effect)
- This leads to... (shows chain)
- Therefore... (conclusion)
dictation: Sometimes, one cause leads to many effects.
Or many causes lead to one effect.
This is called a CHAIN REACTION.
